findings.title: SNMP reachable with public community
findings.description: Host 198.51.100.20 answered SNMP community "public" (Polycom VVX 411 conference phone).
findings.remediation: Change or disable the default SNMP community; restrict UDP/161 to management hosts; prefer SNMPv3 with auth.
findings.unknown: Whether the community also allows writes was not tested.

evidence.summary: Answered an SNMPv2c GET with community "public"; sysDescr "Polycom VVX 411 conference phone"

findings.title: SMB file sharing port open
findings.description: Port 445 is Windows/Samba file sharing. Normal for NAS boxes and PCs that share folders.
findings.remediation: Disable SMBv1; require signing; limit share permissions; patch the host.
findings.unknown: Share permissions, SMB version, and signing were not checked.

findings.title: Remote Desktop (RDP) port open
findings.description: Port 3389 is Windows Remote Desktop, which gives full control of the machine to anyone who can log in.
findings.remediation: Restrict RDP to trusted hosts/VPN; enable NLA; use strong accounts or disable if unused.
findings.unknown: Whether Network Level Authentication is on and how strong the accounts are were not checked.

findings.title: Microsoft SQL Server port open
findings.description: A database reachable from the whole LAN is worth confirming as intended.
findings.remediation: Restrict to trusted hosts; disable unused SQL Browser exposure; use strong auth.
findings.unknown: Accounts and which hosts may connect were not checked.

findings.title: Windows RPC (MSRPC) port open
findings.description: Normal on Windows machines; used by remote management tools.
findings.remediation: Firewall 135 from untrusted hosts; prefer VPN/admin jump hosts for management.

findings.title: NetBIOS session port open
findings.description: Legacy NetBIOS file sharing, often alongside SMB.
findings.remediation: Disable NetBIOS where unused; prefer SMB over 445 with signing; restrict with firewall rules.

findings.title: Raw printer port (9100) open
findings.description: Many network printers accept print jobs on TCP 9100 without a login.
findings.remediation: Place printers on a restricted VLAN; disable unused raw printing; require authenticated print protocols when possible.

findings.title: HTTP (cleartext) port open
findings.description: Web pages on port 80 are not encrypted. Avoid logging in to admin pages over it.
findings.remediation: Prefer HTTPS; avoid sending credentials over HTTP; restrict admin UIs.
findings.unknown: Only the TCP port answered. The software behind it, its version, and whether it asks for a login were not checked.
